brief: Our own block — rows 79..87, the bottom ~15% of every wide shot, the nearest thing in the picture — is 1095 cells of one tile. buildGrid's last branch is `wellAt(x,y) ? VOID : WALL`, so the block is WALL end to end (2441 WALL cells in the whole town; ours is 45% of them) apart from the river slot and 12 VOID cells in two light wells. Everything a roof needs to be a PLACE is already built and nothing human uses it: `roofWalkZ()` reads the pitch bilinearly for a walker, `nearScale(y)` ramps a figure to NEAR_SZ 1.95 — nearly twice the size of anyone across the lane — `ROOF_FURN` stands 24 washing lines, water tanks and pigeon lofts on rows 86-87, `LOFTS` are landing boards, `wellNear(x)` keeps a line off a hole, and `catA` already crosses on `catLine`. Twenty-four things a tenant would own, and in 169 iterations no person has ever stood among them. GIVE THE BLOCK A TOP. Cut a new tile (call it LEADS) — flat lead roof-terrace — into rows 86..87 of some of the bays, sited where the pitch is ALREADY level so no volume changes: the source's own measurement is row 87 dead level across the whole block, row 86 level to within 0.31 of a cell, against z 1.98/1.55 out on the open pitch at rows 84/85. It is WALL to `buildVolumes()` and takes its own fill in the ground cache — GLASS (line ~283) is the exact precedent for a tile with its own volume rule — and it joins `developed` in `__census()` so nothing collapses. Then put a TENANT on it, with their own source and their own cap: up out of a loft hatch to hang the washing, out to take it in when `raining` or `isWindy()` says so, out to stand at the parapet in the evening. A 150-300 line diff is expected and welcome. This is the bet.
successLooksLike: On a fine afternoon a figure stands on our own roof at the bottom of the wide shot, twice the size of anyone in the town, and when the rain comes on they come out and take the washing in. CENSUS OBLIGATION: `tileKinds` 153 -> 162 (a new kind is +9 in the summed 3x3 matrix) and `structures` up by the hatches; `developed` stays at 71730 because LEADS is built ground, and no other scalar collapses. Re-pin with `census.mjs --save-baseline` and SAY SO in the ledger.
avoid: drawNearRoof is inside the GROUND CACHE: the leads belong in the cache, the tenant does NOT — register at cache time, repaint live. `eaveFor()` returns 0 for y >= LN_WALK_S for a DRAWING reason and `shCast[]` (#151) is the casting height beside it: change neither. A new walkable region south of the lane must not become an ordinary route target — give the tenant its own spawn and keep the cells out of every existing target set. Do not put terrace on rows 84/85 and do not cross a light well; `wellNear(x)` exists for exactly that. Do not add a third well.
